title: Quaint Smoky Mexican Cheese Mole Poblano
description: A smoky, cheese-pull, nostalgic Mexican dish featuring malai, reduced to perfection, without onion or garlic, in the form of mole poblano, served on a comal.
instructions: Start by toasting the ancho chilies on a comal over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side.
Remove the chilies from the heat and let them cool down before stemming and seeding them.
In a blender, combine the cooled chilies, malai, chicken broth, almonds, raisins, cinnamon, cocoa powder, salt, and black pepper, and blend until smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a saucepan and bring it to a simmer over low heat.
Reduce the mixture by half, stirring occasionally, which should take about 20 minutes.
While the mixture is reducing, prepare the comal by heating it over medium heat and brushing it with a little bit of oil.
Once the mixture has reduced, stir in the shredded cheese until it is fully melted and the mixture is smooth.
Pour the cheese mixture onto the prepared comal and let it cook for 2 minutes, until the bottom is lightly browned and the cheese is melted and bubbly.
Use a spatula to carefully lift and fold the edges of the cheese mixture towards the center, allowing the uncooked cheese to flow to the edges and cook.
Repeat the lifting and folding process for about 5 minutes, until the cheese is fully cooked and has a nice browned crust on the bottom.
